question: What is the very first priority when a patient arrives in the emergency department with a severe laceration?
explanation: General patient stability and life-threatening issues always come before treating localized injuries like skin lacerations. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is it important to test movement and feeling in the fingers or toes below a wound before stitching it?

options.A: To make the skin easier to numb with medication
options.B: To prevent the wound from becoming infected later
options.C: To see if the patient is allergic to local anesthetics
options.D: To check if nerves and blood vessels were damaged by the injury

explanation: Testing distal motor and sensory function helps catch nerve or vessel damage early, before any repair work begins. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which medication is most commonly used as a local anesthetic for closing minor wounds?
explanation: Lignocaine numbs the local area quickly and safely when administered correctly before suturing. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h2)

question: Where should a nurse NOT use a local anesthetic mixed with adrenaline?
explanation: Adrenaline causes blood vessels to constrict tightly, which can cut off blood supply entirely in digits and lead to tissue death. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of irrigating a fresh wound with normal saline?

options.A: To wash away bacteria and loose debris
options.C: To close the skin edges tightly
options.D: To stop bleeding from large arteries

explanation: High-volume fluid irrigation physically flushes out contaminants that could otherwise cause a localized infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why do emergency personnel perform debridement on a ragged, torn wound before stitching it?

options.A: It makes the skin numb to the pain of the needle
options.B: Dead tissue delays healing and easily breeds bacteria
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling nervous
options.D: It stretches the skin so fewer stitches are needed

explanation: Removing non-viable tissue leaves only healthy, bleeding tissue that can heal rapidly and resist infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which type of needle is best suited for piercing tough, thick outer skin?
explanation: Cutting needles have a sharp edge specifically designed to pass through tough dermal layers without bending. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h4)

question: A patient requires skin closure on a forehead laceration that will need stitches removed in five days. Which suture type should the nurse prepare?
explanation: Skin surface closures require non-absorbable materials like nylon so they remain intact until manual removal. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the most common and versatile suturing technique used for simple emergency lacerations?
explanation: Simple interrupted stitches are quick to place and provide reliable closure where each stitch stands alone. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why should a surgical knot be positioned to the side of the wound incision rather than directly over it?

options.A: To make it easier for the patient to pull out later
options.B: To prevent pressure on the wound line that can slow healing
options.C: To ensure the local anesthetic stays active longer
options.D: To save suture material during the procedure

explanation: Placing knots off-center prevents direct pressure and irritation on the healing skin edge underneath. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of normal wound healing that a patient should expect?

options.A: A thin line of pinkness near the cut
options.B: Pus draining from the incision site
options.C: Dry scabbing along the suture line

explanation: Pus indicates a bacterial infection and is never a normal part of wound healing. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why do facial stitches need to be removed much sooner than stitches on a knee or back?

options.A: Facial skin is much thicker than skin on the back
options.B: The face heals faster due to a rich blood supply
options.C: Stitches on the face cause less scarring if left longer
options.D: Facial muscles do not move during daily activities

explanation: The abundant blood supply in the head and neck allows rapid healing, requiring early suture removal to prevent track marks. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h6)
